accuracy.evidence: The sympathy/empathy distinction follows the psychology usage (feeling for versus understanding and sharing another's state) and Brené Brown's summary of Theresa Wiseman's (1996) four attributes: perspective-taking, staying out of judgement, recognising emotion and communicating it. Reflecting and paraphrasing follow Carl Rogers' person-centred active listening (say back content and feeling, then check). Compassion fatigue signs (numbness, dread, poor sleep, irritability) follow Figley's description for carers and are stated as warning signs, not a diagnosis. The safeguarding line (safety worries go to a trusted adult even if a secret was promised) matches DfE Keeping Children Safe in Education and PSHE Association guidance. Numeric items were checked at the corners of their ranges, including the where clause on p4.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips adolescents and adults make when comforting: the silver lining 'at least' (step 1 prediction, step 2, challenge 'least', m2), pity from a distance (step 1 'poor you', challenge 'pity', m1), telling someone how to feel (step 2 'Don't be sad'), jumping to advice (step 2, step 4 'fix', challenge 'fix', p5), turning the talk to yourself (step 4 'me', m3), echoing instead of paraphrasing (step 4 'parrot', challenge 'echo', p5), closed questions (step 3 prediction, challenge 'closed', p3), empathy as agreement (challenge 'agree', m1), and the opposite error that a good friend must always be available or keep a safety secret (step 5 prediction, challenge 'secret' and 'alone', m6, m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagempa is built on five listening mechanics specific to empathy at 12-13: a hole-and-ladder where only empathic replies move you down to Jas, striking minimising lines in a draft with a 'how heard' meter, a talk meter that grows only with open questions, choosing reflections over echo, advice and self-focus, and finding compassion-fatigue signs in a helper's week with an energy bar. flagothers (ages 5-8) only sorts four replies into two bins; flagpal (14-16) spots a struggling friend's changes, orders a talk and sorts secrets. lab_distinct gate passes under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the difference rather than reading it: 'At least you'll get a bigger bedroom' leaves You at the top of the hole while 'That sounds really hard' moves you down; closed questions get 'Yeah, fine' and 'Mm' while open ones fill Jas's bubble and the meter; each crossed-out line raises the 'how heard Jas feels' bar. Feedback names why each rejected reply fails before the text sums up the rule.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: that 'At least…' cheers her up and so is empathy (the hole refuses it as a silver lining), that 'Are you OK?' gets Jas talking (she answers 'Yeah, fine'), and that a good friend must be there for everyone all the time (Kai's week shows the cost, and the Sunday boundary is marked healthy).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages: least, pity, closed, echo, fix, same, agree, normal, adult, secret and alone, each naming the specific slip.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs read at about FK grade 3 to 5 with one idea each and quoted example phrases; the adult text was rewritten into short sentences (about grade 6) while keeping the terms sympathy, empathy, perspective-taking, active listening, reflecting, paraphrasing, minimising, compassion fatigue and boundary. Canvas replies are one short quoted line each.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph covers one part of the topic (definition, minimising, listening skills, protecting yourself and safety); items each test a different point: empathic reply (p1), listening ratio (p2), open question (p3), helper energy (p4), reflection (p5), definition (m1), minimising (m2), self-focus (m3), open-question payoff (m4), fatigue sign (m5), boundary (m6), safeguarding (m7) and the load of helping (m8).

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and dark and iPhone 13 dark screenshots of every step at start, mid-demo and after Show me: Jas's line, the hole with rungs and both figures fit beside each other after moving You to the right of the hole; three reply cards wrap to two lines; seven draft lines and seven diary lines fit under their meters; the six questions sit in a 2 by 3 grid below Jas's bubble; challenge buttons wrap at phone width.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'Reply: …', 'Cross out: …', 'Ask: …', 'Reflect: …' and 'Warning sign? …' with the full diary text. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback message, including Jas's answers. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
